skill.name: type-safety-validation
skill.description: Guide for building end-to-end TypeScript type safety with Zod runtime validation, tRPC APIs, Prisma data access, and strict compiler features.
skill.summary: Build validated TypeScript applications from database models to API clients and user interfaces.
skill.author: AI Agent Hub

security_audit.summary: All 36 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown syntax, TypeScript examples, sample URLs, relative imports, validation chains, and ordinary identifiers. One medium semantic issue remains: the examples expose database reads and writes without authentication or authorization.

remediation.issue: API examples expose user lookup and post creation without access control.
remediation.suggestion: Use authenticated procedures, enforce role and ownership checks, and explain authorization requirements before each database read or write.

content.value_statement: Static types alone cannot verify data arriving at application boundaries. This skill shows how Zod, tRPC, Prisma, and TypeScript connect compile-time types with runtime validation.
actual_capabilities: Defines Zod schemas with refinements, transformations, unions, recursive types, and inferred TypeScript types.
Shows typed tRPC procedures and clients with Zod input validation.
Demonstrates Prisma models, typed queries, relations, and nested record creation.
Explains modern TypeScript features including const parameters, satisfies, decorators, and strict compiler options.
Combines Next.js, tRPC, Prisma, and React in an end-to-end example.
limitations: Provides guidance and examples but does not inspect repositories, run checks, or install dependencies.
The full-stack example is incomplete and needs authentication, authorization, error handling, and production configuration.
Library APIs and TypeScript features may change, so verify examples against installed versions.
Focuses on Zod, tRPC, Prisma, Next.js, and React rather than every validation or API framework.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Validation Schema
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Zod schema for {data shape}. Include validation rules, an inferred TypeScript type, and safeParse error handling.
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin with runtime validation for one data object.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Typed Procedure
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a tRPC procedure for {operation}. Validate its input with Zod and describe the inferred client types and expected errors.
prompt_templates.scenario: Add a validated API operation to an existing service.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Type-Safety Boundary
prompt_templates.prompt: Review {boundary or workflow} for unsafe inputs, any usage, missing checks, and type duplication. Recommend focused Zod and TypeScript improvements.
prompt_templates.scenario: Assess an existing form, endpoint, integration, or database workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Plan End-to-End Type Safety
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a migration of {application} to strict TypeScript, Zod, tRPC, and Prisma. Prioritize boundaries, compatibility risks, tests, and incremental delivery.
prompt_templates.scenario: Coordinate an advanced migration across database, server, and client layers.

output_examples.input: Validate a registration form with email, age, and role fields.
output_examples.output: A Zod schema validates email format, age limits, and allowed roles. The result includes an inferred form type and field-level error guidance.

output_examples.input: Design a typed endpoint that loads a user by identifier.
output_examples.output: The proposed procedure validates the identifier before querying. It explains nullable results, client inference, authorization requirements, and safe error handling.

output_examples.input: Review a JavaScript service before a strict TypeScript migration.
output_examples.output: The review prioritizes external inputs, database results, unchecked indexes, and broad any types. It proposes phased compiler changes and boundary validation.

best_practices: Validate untrusted data at every external boundary and return clear, structured errors.
Infer types from shared schemas to reduce duplicated declarations and drift.
Enable strict compiler checks gradually and protect each migration step with tests.
anti_patterns: Do not treat compile-time types as proof that runtime data is valid.
Do not expose database procedures without authentication, authorization, and ownership checks.
Do not use broad any types or unchecked casts to silence migration errors.

faq.question: Does this skill run type checks on my project?
faq.answer: No. It provides implementation guidance and examples, but it does not execute compilers or inspect files automatically.

faq.question: Can I use Zod without tRPC or Prisma?
faq.answer: Yes. Each library can be used independently, although the examples show how they support one typed application flow.

faq.question: Does TypeScript replace runtime validation?
faq.answer: No. TypeScript checks source code, while runtime validation verifies values from users, networks, files, and other external systems.

faq.question: Are the examples production ready?
faq.answer: No. Add authentication, authorization, logging controls, error handling, tests, rate limits, and environment-specific configuration.

faq.question: Which TypeScript settings are recommended?
faq.answer: Start with strict mode and consider noUncheckedIndexedAccess. Adopt additional checks according to project compatibility and migration cost.

faq.question: How should validation errors reach users?
faq.answer: Map schema issues to stable field or request errors. Avoid exposing internal database details, stack traces, or sensitive input values.
